(ii) Verbal Warning in 2022
In June 2022, our Company and two of our then senior management, namely, Mr. Li
and Mr. Yang Fangyan (then chief financial officer and then secretary of the Board) received
a verbal warning (the “2022 Verbal Warning”) from the NEEQ for an error in the accounting
of our consolidated financial statements, whereby figures including, among others, the
revenue, cost of sales, expenses, net profit were adjusted and as a result we over-distributed
dividend in the sum of RMB10,277,280.86 for the six months ended June 30, 2017 (the “2017
Accounting Adjustment”). As excessive distribution of dividend cannot be rectified, the
distributable profit for the financial year ended December 31, 2021 was reduced accordingly
because of the error. As we were preparing for our A-share Application, we appointed a new
reporting accountant. In the course of preparing the financial statements for the year ended
December 31, 2020, our then auditor identified and recommended the correction of the
financial figures.
Thedetailsof theadjustmentsaresetforthbelow:(i)Thetimingof revenuerecognition
for DDU and DDP business arrangements were adjusted to delivery of goods to the
customer’s destination, instead of customers’ acknowledgement of delivery of goods to the
customer’s destination. This had led to a reduction of approximately RMB14.2 million in
operating income and a reduction of RMB12.0 million in operating costs for the year 2020;
and as at the end of 2020, accounts receivable decreased by RMB12.4 million and inventories
increased by RMB10.3 million. These adjustments resulted in changes in the amount of
revenueandcostsof salesoverdifferentreportingperiods,butdidnotresultinchangestothe
cumulative revenue and costs of sales recognized. (ii) At the recommendation of the then
auditors, considering that the Company and SDMC HK (subsidiary of the Company) are
separate legal entities who formed creditor-debtor relationship with the supply chain
company which provides custom export services, receivables of the Company from a supply
chain company and payables by SDMC HK to the same supply chain company shall not be
offset and were reversed. This had led to an increase of approximately RMB94.5 million in
accountsreceivableandanincreaseof approximatelyRMB97.7millioninaccountspayableat
the consolidated financial statement as at the end of 2020; and revenue increased by
approximately RMB6.6 million and operating costs increased by approximately RMB5.9
million at the consolidated financial statement of the Company in 2020. These consolidation
offsets and reverses were mainly due to differences in understanding of the relevant
accounting treatment among different auditing institutions, and the relevant adjustments did
not have a material adverse impact on the Company’s operating net profit. (iii) As the foreign
currency transactions were recorded in RMB based on the customs exchange rate,
adjustments were made to using their original currency and spot exchange rate. This had led
to a reduction of approximately RMB6.3 million in accounts receivable and a decrease of
approximately RMB1.6 million in accounts payable as at the end of 2020, and financial
expenses increased by approximately RMB4.3 million for the year 2020.
In view of the foregoing, the main adjustment to the financial statements for the year
2020were:(i)decreaseinnetprofitof approximatelyRMB10.2million,or17.1%;(ii)increase
in total assets as of December 31, 2020 of approximately RMB86.5 million, or 15.3%; (iii)
increase in total liabilities of approximately RMB98.8 million, or 28.8%; and (iv) decrease in
net assets of approximately RMB12.2 million or 5.5%.

held by the public. Under Rule 19A.13A(1) of the Listing Rules, in the event the expected
market value of the Company’s H Shares upon Listing does not exceed HK$6 billion, at least
25%of thetotalissuedHSharesmustbeheldbythepublicuponListing,andtheCompany’s
expected public float of 52.37% will satisfy the minimum requirement of 25%. Should the
expected market value exceeds HK$6.00 billion but not exceeding HK$30.00 billion, the
minimumpublicfloatrequirementisthehigherof (i)15%of thetotalissuedHSharesand(ii)
such percentage of the total issued H Shares as would result in the expected market value of
the H Shares held by the public being at least HK$1.50 billion upon Listing; in this scenario,
the Company’s expected public float of 52.37% exceeds the 15% threshold, and the market
valueof suchHSharesheldbythepublicwouldalsoexceedtheHK$1.50billionrequirement
(e.g., approximately HK$3.60 billion based on the Offer Price of HK$32.8 per Offer Share).
Therefore, the Company will be able to meet the minimum public float requirement Rule 8.08
(as amended and replaced by Rule 19A.13A) of the Listing Rules upon Listing in either
scenario.
FREE FLOAT
Based on an Offer Price of HK$32.80 per H Share, the Company will satisfy the free
float requirement under Rule 19A.13C of the Listing Rules.

HISTORY AND CORPORATE STRUCTURE

BUSINESS
OVERVIEW
We are a provider of smart home products for enterprise customers, focused on
enhancing home applications through intelligent technologies. The smart home products we
offer include both hardware and software products. During the Track Record Period, our
revenue was mainly generated from sales of hardware products, namely our digital video
devices and network communication devices. Smart home products refer to an integrated
home ecosystem that connects and manages various smart devices across the household,
enabling whole-home network coverage and device interaction. Different from smart home
product providers who sell self-branded products directly to consumers, we, as a provider of
smart home products for enterprise customers, develop and sell digital video devices and
network communication devices with our customers’ brands, and provide system platforms
and services, to enterprise customers. Our solutions allow users to control their home with
ease leveraging the application of cloud, IoT and AI technologies, through our digital video
devices, such as media streaming terminals, speakers, projectors, and cameras, network
communication devices, such as optical network terminals, Wi-Fi routers, and cable modems,
andsystemplatforms,suchasCedar,XHomeandXMediaTV.AccordingtoFrost&Sullivan,
we are the eighth largest provider globally, and the third largest among Chinese
Mainland-basedproviders,intheglobalsmarthomeproductforenterprisecustomersmarket
intermsof revenuein2024,withamarketshareof 2.7%.Intermsof marketsizein2024,the
global enterprise smart home product market accounts for approximately 14.7% of the entire
global smart home product market.
Founded in 2003 by entrepreneur Mr. Li Bo, our odyssey commenced with the
developmentandsalesof cryptographicchips.Intheyearsthatfollowed,wesetfootindigital
TV modules and TV dongles. In 2012, we launched AOSP-based digital video solutions, and
started partnering with overseas telecom operators. As a testament to our technical
capabilities, we became one of the first companies in China to secure a Google Android TV
certification in 2017 and the first ODM company worldwide to secure a Google TV projector
certificationin2023,whichprovedourtechnologicalcapabilityandfosteredthedevelopment
of projectors with copyright content in overseas markets, and brought us business
opportunities to establish cooperation with Google TV projector brand owners. Per Frost &
Sullivan, we are the world’s largest Android TV smart terminal supplier measured by sales
volume in 2024.
Capitalizing on our expertise in digital video devices, we have strategically expanded
into system platforms and network communication businesses. In 2017, we launched
XMediaTV, a media streaming platform, followed by a full-scale penetration into network
infrastructurestartingin2020offeringcarrier-gradeWi-Firouters,opticalnetworkterminals
(ONTs), and cable modems. The same year saw the launch of XHome, a home device
management platform, reinforcing our expertise in hardware-software integration.
The emergence and maturing of AI has driven the shift from “smart home” to “AI
Home” — a transition from passive responsiveness to proactive services, enhancing
convenience, energy efficiency, security, health management and cross-device synergy with
intelligent,personalizedandautomatedtechnologies.Meanwhile,Matterhasbecomeamajor
standard for smart home devices that enable greater interoperability across different
ecosystems.In2024,penetrationrateof Mattergloballyhasreachedapproximately30%,and
is expected to further increase to 50% by 2030.
To address this trend, we have accelerated the development of our products. Our
network communication and digital video devices have been upgraded with features such as
Matterconnectivity,edgecomputingandenvironmentsensing.In2024,weintroducedCedar,
a home agent supported by third-party large language models. Cedar has completed its
researchanddevelopmentandisreadyformassproduction.Asof theLatestPracticableDate,

Cedar is in the customer testing and commercialization stage, where we provide samples or
solution prototypes to potential customers for functional testing and scenario adaptation,
which forms part of our standard market introduction process rather than the research and
development phase. We are currently in business discussions with certain telecom operators,
and expect Cedar to begin generating revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026. We collaborate
with OEM partners to develop Matter-compliant IoT devices and work with telecom
operators to support smart home deployments, enabling us to provide integrated smart home
productscombininghardwareandsoftware.Leveragingthird-partylargelanguagemodels,we
have developed application features for smart home scenarios, and Cedar supports functions
suchasvisualrecognition,semanticunderstandingandnaturallanguageinteraction,enabling
userstoanalyzeimagescapturedbydevicesandcontrolhomeappliancesthroughvoiceortext
commands. We have adapted these models to better suit home environments and integrated
themwithourXHomeplatform,allowingcoordinateddevicemanagementandcontrolwithin
a unified system.
Driven by technological innovation and evolving user demands, the global digital and
intelligent home solutions market is undergoing a profound transformation — from digital
home to smart home. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global smart home products market
has surged from US$53.5 billion in 2020 to US$88.6 billion in 2024, with a CAGR of 13.4%
from 2020 to 2024. Propelled by continuous function enrichment and performance
improvement of smart home hardware combined with escalating consumer demand for
higher-configuration smart home terminals and advanced networking solutions, the global
smart home products market is projected to reach US$238.2 billion in 2029, representing a
CAGRof 21.9%from2024to2029.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriod,weprimarilysoldsmart
home products and solutions, which accounted for 75.3%, 73.6% and 80.8% of our total
revenue for 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
Our Ecosystem
Our ecosystem is composed of system platforms, network communication devices,
digital video devices, and an open-ended device matrix that can connect with foreign devices,
together forming an open ecosystem. This open ecosystem seamlessly integrates software and
hardware and enables autonomous perception, learning and interaction.
– 141 –

=== PAGE 151 ===
BUSINESS
• Software: Our system platforms comprise our Home AI agent Cedar, our media
streaming platform XMediaTV and our home device management platform
XHome. Leveraging Gemini, Cedar serves as a cognitive decision-making nucleus
that analyzes and processes data, executes high-precision intent recognition, and
issuescontext-awareactioncommandsviaXMediaTVandXHome.Thesesystem
platforms together control various connected devices to address user needs in
different application scenarios.
• Hardware: Our network communication devices, encompassing Wi-Fi routers,
ONTs and cable modems, ensures high-speed, ultra-stable whole-home Internet
coverage. Our digital video devices include media streaming terminals,
projectors, cameras and AI speaker. In addition, as of the Latest Practicable
Date, we had other AI-powered products in the pipeline such as robots, AI
glasses, AI photo frame and AI computing box designed for users’entertainment
and companionship. With edge computing, environment sensing and Matter
compatibility, our hardware products function as home hubs.
• Openecosystem:OurhomeecosystemfeaturesanopenecosystembuiltonMatter
protocol. It offers cross-ecosystem, cross-brand interoperability, which brings
multi-vendor devices under our single management and automation umbrella,
allowing open-ended device scalability. The integration of diverse
Matter-compliantdevicesfurtherimprovesoursmarthomeapplicationscenarios
and enriches user experience.
In this ecosystem, system platforms undertake data analysis, reasoning and
decision-making, and dispatch commands to digital video devices and network
communication devices. Our digital video devices and network communication devices, as
home hubs, integrating the Matter protocol, can thus relay the commands to other
Matter-compliant devices. Digital video devices, network communication devices, and other
Matter-compliantdevicesinreturnfeeduserandenvironmentaldatabacktosystemplatforms
for iterative learning and further analysis. This way, users, environment and devices are
interconnected and smart home living experience with autonomous perception, learning, and
interaction are delivered.
Our Key Clients
As of December 31, 2025, we served more than 300 clients across over 80 countries and
regions around the globe, with a focus on telecom operators. We have established long-term,
stable collaborative relationships with major telecom operators in Europe, North America,
Latin America and Asia, many of which are Fortune Global 500 enterprises, including
renowned multinational telecom operator giants, and top-ranked telecom operators in 13
regional markets. In addition, we also provide ODM services for retailers.
Our Production Model
Weadoptanasset-lightproductionstrategy,leveraginglong-standingpartnershipswith
top hardware manufacturers in the world and our rich experience in supply chain
management. Our globally distributed supply chain enables us to pick the right manufacturer
according to client needs, ensuring agility, cost efficiency and resilience against geopolitical
risks.

COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS
Well-positioned in the Thriving Smart Home Product Market
The smart home market has experienced exponential growth in recent years, fueled by
relentless advancements in IoT and network technologies. According to Frost & Sullivan, the
globalsmarthomeproductsmarketsurgedfromUS$53.5billionin2020toUS$88.6billionin
2024, reflecting a CAGR of 13.4% from 2020 to 2024. Within this expansion, the smart home
devices sector escalated from US$37.5 billion in 2020 to US$65.6 billion in 2024; the smart
homeinfrastructuresectorgrewfromUS$15.0billionin2020toUS$18.6billionin2024;and
the system platforms sector rose from US$1.0 billion in 2020 to US$4.4 billion in 2024.
Propelled by continuous function enrichment and performance improvement of smart home
hardware and escalating consumer demand for higher-configuration smart home terminals
andadvancednetworkingsolutions,theglobalsmarthomeproductsmarketisprojectedreach
US$238.2 billion in 2029, representing a CAGR of 21.9% from 2024 to 2029.
To catch this trend, we have accelerated the development and advancement of our
products. Our network infrastructure and digital video products have now evolved to feature
Matter connectivity, edge computing and environment sensing, and functioning as cognitive
home hubs. In 2024, we unveiled our Gemini-powered Home AI agent Cedar. According to
Frost & Sullivan, we are the eighth largest provider globally, and the third largest among
Chinese Mainland-based providers, in the global smart home product for enterprise
customers market in terms of revenue in 2024. In terms of market size in 2024, the global
enterprise smart home product market accounts for approximately 14.7% of the entire global
smart home product market.
Ourmaindigitalvideoproducts—AndroidTVsmartmediastreamingterminals—are
important constituents of the smart home market. Google certification is an indispensable
conditionforentryintheAndroidTVterminalmarket,athresholdwecrossedin2017asone
of China’s inaugural Google Android TV-certified enterprises. In 2023, we became the first
ODM company worldwide to secure the Google TV projector certification. According to

High-Caliber R&D Team and Innovation Capabilities Translating Technologies into Integrated
Smart Home Products
Since inception, we have been closely tracking market demands and technological
frontiers and cultivated a high-caliber R&D team. We focus on development and
accumulation of proprietary core technologies. We have established comprehensive R&D
system based on our core technologies while encompassing core principles of “technological
innovation,standardizedR&Dandagiledelivery.”ThroughcontinuousinnovationandR&D
activities, we achieve technological breakthroughs and gained standardized, modular
capabilities, forming a reusable technology platform. Agile delivery relies on platform
capabilities to quickly respond to customized needs, enabling efficient product iteration and
valuerealization.Thesethreecoreprinciplesformaclosed-loopsystem,ultimatelycreatinga
virtuous cycle that continues to power our R&D efficiency and prowess.
We believe R&D talent is crucial to our technological prowess and business success.
Through years of strategic blend of internal cultivation and global recruitment, we have
formed a well-structured R&D team with experienced talent who possess multidimensional,
balanced competencies in technology development, cross-functional team collaboration and
complex technical problem-solving. As of December 31, 2025, we had over 400 R&D talent,
representing over 60% of our total workforce.
We improve smart living experience through hardware innovation. We have core
proprietarytechnologiesinhardware,softwareandedgealgorithms,achievingintelligentand
high performance product and rapid iterations. In the network communication domain, we
have developed Mesh multi-scenario converged networking technology, seamless Wi-Fi
connectiontechnology,MatterIoTconnectivityandcross-protocolinteroperability,elevating
user experience in whole-home Internet coverage, zero-latency roaming and device
connectivity. In the field of digital video devices, we have built a complete audio and video
technology system covering core technologies including streaming media decoding, optical
and color correction, AI super-resolution enhancement, far-field noise reduction, and speech
recognition, supporting and providing a cinema-grade graphic quality and an immersive
interactive experience.
Our proprietary software solutions transforms connectivity into cognition. XMediaTV
is our media streaming platform, which realizes personalized recommendations for content
and services for home users, and provides support for marketing decisions and improves user
conversion rate for global operators. XHome provides zero-touch provisioning and wide
spectrum of IoT solutions spanning from device management, device maintenance, smart
scenarios, multi-screen client, operation management, to data center, helping telecom
operatorsandretailersbuildadifferentiatedecosystem.Cedarasacognitivedecision-making
nucleus analyzes household data, executes accurate intent recognition and issues
context-aware commands via XMediaTV and XHome, controlling various connected devices
to address user needs in different application scenarios.
By connecting Cedar with our digital video devices and network communication
devices, we enhance its AI capabilities and achieve edge-AI synergy, providing personalized,
interactive user experience in various smart home scenarios.
We believe our excellent R&D team and this hardware-software innovation approach
enable us to provide integrated smart home products to our clients, keep up with industry
development trends and quickly respond to client needs, thereby consolidating our market
position. We believe our R&D philosophy effectively transforms technology into seamless
intelligent experiences that anticipate tomorrow’s living paradigms.

BUSINESS
Robust Supply Chain Capabilities and High-quality Client Base
Guided by an unwavering proactive market strategy, we have cultivated profound
partnerships with our key accounts. We have established enduring collaborations with global
telecomoperators—ourcoreclientele,byprovidingone-stopservicesencompassingproduct
R&D and design, manufacturing and after-sales management, effectively enhancing client
retention through value-driven engagement. Leveraging our acute market intelligence, robust
R&D capabilities and globally distributed supply chain network, we maintain exceptional
agility to evolving market demands, enabling swift new product commercialization.
Our supply chain management capabilities are built upon an integrated global
procurement and production system:
• Rawmaterials:Wehaveestablishedavastsuppliernetworkconsistingof over800
vetted suppliers across 12 countries and regions, which ensures a stable supply of
raw materials. Our core raw materials are procured from prestigious suppliers
who can meet our rigorous quality requirements at reasonable costs, laying a
foundation for the reliable, timely deliveries and competitive price of our
products.
• Production: We adopt an asset-light production model in partnership with
well-known OEMs based in various countries and regions in the world. This
unique model brings manufacturing agility — allowing us to achieve economies
of scale for large-volume orders, while maintaining flexible production capacity
for diverse, small-batch requests.
Our global supply chain can effectively reduce lead times by choosing the right raw
materials suppliers and OEMs in the right places to ensure timely delivery, and mitigate
geopolitical risks in this changing trade environment through the globally distributed

OUR BUSINESS MODEL
We provide smart home products that allow users to control their home with ease
leveraging the application of cloud, IoT and AI technologies in the home setting, through (i)
our digital video devices, such as media streaming terminals, speakers, projectors, and
cameras, (ii) our network communication devices, such as optical network terminals, Wi-Fi
routers, and cable modems, and (iii) our system platforms, namely our home AI agent Cedar,
our media streaming platform XMediaTV and our home device management platform
XHome, which serve as the decision-making and control center to operate, manage and
maintain digital video devices and network communication devices. During the Track Record
Period,ourrevenuewasmainlygeneratedfromsalesof hardwareproducts,namelyourdigital
video devices and network communication devices. Our end enterprise customers are
primarily telecom operators and retailers.
During the Track Record Period, we sold our products and solutions to end enterprise
customers both directly and indirectly through intermediaries, including trading companies,
manufacturers and other smart home product providers. In our earlier stage, certain
customers transacted through intermediaries, while as our business developed, we
increasingly established direct sales relationships. Under the direct sales model, customers
place orders and make payments to us directly, whereas under the indirect model,
intermediaries place orders with us and sele payments on behalf of the end customers. We
cooperated with 10, nine and 18 intermediaries under the indirect sales model in 2023, 2024
and 2025, respectively.
Since 2010 and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we have cumulatively delivered smart
home products, comprising end-to-end hardware and software solutions, to over 300 global
telecom operators and retailers, serving millions of households worldwide.
Wecontinuetoenhanceourpresenceinthefieldof homesolutions.Startingin2023,we
leverage the application of AI technology and machine learning to empower our smart home
products to learn, adapt and make autonomous decisions based on user behavior and
environmental context, creating a more proactive and self-sufficient living environment. In
particular, network communication devices establish the basic network connection for the
entire home, while digital video devices enable home users to experience smart home
applications. Furthermore, we have enhanced the connectivity and inclusiveness of our smart
home products by adopting Matter, an industry standard protocol for smart homes designed
toeliminatecompatibilityissues,simplifydevicesetupandconnectivity,andincreasesecurity
and reliability, edge computing allowing the capture, processing, and analysis of data at the

OUR ECOSYSTEM
We are committed to a deep integration of software platform, hardware device, and an
openecosystem,providingintegratedsmarthomeproductswithself-perception,self-learning
and self-interaction. Our ecosystem comprises our system platform (system layer), network
communicationdevices,digitalvideodevices(hardwarelayer),andouropenecosystembased
onMatterprotocol(ecosystemlayer),leveragingourindustryexpertise,deliveringend-to-end
AI-powered smart living services across the entire home.
At the system layer, we have established an architecture centered on Cedar, our Home
AIagent,synergizingwithXMediaTV,ourmediastreamingplatform,andXHome,ourhome
device management platform. Cedar achieves high-precision intent recognition through
multimodal data analysis of voice, habits, images and sensor data, driving XMediaTV and
XHome to accurately execute audio-visual recommendations, device control, environmental
adjustments, and cybersecurity settings. This ensures fulfillment of user needs across diverse
application scenarios, significantly enhancing smart living experiences.
At the hardware layer, our network communication devices enable high-speed, stable
and whole-home network coverage, while our digital video devices deeply integrates core
scenarios including entertainment, security, energy-saving, and companionship. Certain
hardware has integrated edge computing and environment perception technologies and
evolved into terminals with self-perception and self-learning capabilities.
Attheecosystemlayer,throughthecompatibilityprovidedbyMatterprotocol,someof
our products, namely our digital video devices with Thread modules, or Google TV products
systems have become central hubs for home connectivity, enabling seamless cross-brand and
– 150 –

=== PAGE 160 ===
BUSINESS
cross-ecosystem collaboration. As an open ecosystem protocol, any Matter-enabled device
can interact and operate with other Matter devices from different brands. This enhances
compatibility, allowing devices from various sources to integrate into smart home products,
creating a convenient, interconnected, and collaboratively operated home environment. As
market recognition of the Matter ecosystem grows, our revenue from Matter ecosystem
products has increased significantly. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our revenue generated from
Matter-compliant products accounted for 10.9%, 23.6% and 15.4%, respectively, enhancing
ourstrategicpositioninfutureAIHomeecosystems.Suchproductsrepresentedaminorityof
our total product units sold during the Track Record Period.
Operationally, our system platform conducts comprehensive analysis and reasoning of
home data, transmits appropriate action commands to various terminals via high-speed
networkswhilereceivingreal-timefeedbackfromuserinteractionsandenvironmentalsensing
data. This continuous iteration within the “platform-terminal-environment” loop forms a
closed-loop system, enabling deep synergy among people, objects, and spaces. Ultimately, it
builds an end-to-end, fully autonomous smart home product.
The following diagram illustrates our ecosystem:
OUR TECHNOLOGY INFRASTRUCTURE
Our ecosystem is built around two major subsystems, namely our system platform and
our home hub.
Our system platform can be further split into two key processes — ”thinking” and
“action.” For the “thinking” process, the agent is the main processing unit that handles the
logical reasoning of users’ command. The third-party LLM, on the other hand, processes
users’ commands and interpret the intention of such commands for devices. Meanwhile, the
memory module stores user-specific information such as home users’ habits and past
behaviors, while the planning module studies and summarizes information stored in the
memory module and makes appropriate autonomous decisions based on interaction with the
memory module.
– 151 –

=== PAGE 161 ===
BUSINESS
After the “thinking” process is completed, the command generated from “thinking” is
then translated into “action,” which can be performed by our media streaming platform
XMediaTV,ourdevicemanagementplatformXHome,andcompatiblethird-partyAPIs,such
as those for weather checking.
Another subsystem is our home hub comprising some of our hardware with
edge-computing,environmentsensingandMatter-compatibleconnectivitycapabilities,which
interacts with users directly through intermediaries such as APP interface or voice interface
and handles the environment sensing functions through edge computing to detect changes in
theirsurroundings—e.g.ourOTTTVboxes,smartcameras,andWi-Firoutersarecapableof
environment sensing through images, voice and movement. Such changes are transmitted
through our home hub, which processes the changes, and, in turn, transmits the outcome to
the system platform which will act upon the information transmitted.
Toillustratetheworkflowof ourecosystem,weprovidethefollowingexample.Suppose
thatahomeusersaid“thelightfromthewindowisalittlebitharsh”–thisinformationwould
befirstcapturedbyahomehubsensingdevice,suchasoursmartspeakers,andwouldthenbe
transmitted to the system platform through the network components of the home hub. After
the agent received the information transmitted from the home hub, it would order the
third-partyLLMtoascertaintheintentionof “thelightfromthewindowisalittlebitharsh.”
The agent would then resonate that the user’s home had a smart curtain device, and the harsh
light could be reduced by shutting the curtains. The agent would then start the action after
reaching the conclusion, and would schedule the device platform inside to shut the curtain.
The user’s action would then be recorded and the action would be learned through the
planning module. If the user requested the same operation for many times in a similar time
range, the planning module would consider it as the user’s personal habit.

OUR SOLUTIONS
Our Hardware Solutions — Digital Video Devices and Network Communication Devices
Since 2012, when we successfully developed and launched a series of media streaming
products based on the Android AOSP open-source system, our business has always been
centered on the evolving needs of global telecom operators’ home business, which often
include our projects into their service packages. Over the years, we have been able to expand
our solutions offerings and enhance our solutions capabilities, to provide a combination of
hardware and software solutions. We are capable of customizing our smart home products
based on telecom operators’ different types of smart home businesses and specific needs as
wellashomeusers’preference,benefitingfromourcomprehensiveofferings.Inparticular,our
hardwareofferingscomprisevariousdigitalvideodeviceswithdifferentparameters,including
OTT TV boxes, smart projectors, and smart cameras, and network communication devices,
including Wi-Fi routers, optical network terminals, and cable modems.

BUSINESS
Driven by technological innovation and evolving user demands, the global home
solutions market is undergoing a transition from digital home to more intelligent home
solutions. Some of our digital video and network communication devices incorporate
technologies such as edge computing and advanced algorithms, enabling functions such as
environmental perception, user interaction and coordination with home system applications.
Wehavedevelopedandlaunchedmultipleproductswithenhancedintelligentfeatures.Onthe
hardware side, these products are equipped with advanced chip solutions that support
on-device computing capabilities. On the software side, we utilize a combination of in-house
and third-party algorithms, including those for image enhancement, voice interaction and
network optimization, to improve performance in areas such as image quality, sound effects
and network coverage. In addition, sensing and recognition capabilities enable devices to
respond to environmental changes and support applications such as health monitoring and
home security. These products can also be integrated with our home system platform, Cedar,
which supports functions such as voice interaction, user preference learning, intelligent
recommendations,networkmanagementanddevicecoordination,servingasacentralcontrol
point within the home ecosystem.
The recent ban on foreign-made Wi-Fi routers issued by the U.S. Federal
Communications Commission (FCC) has limited impact on our business, primarily because
(i) our video devices and other network communication devices are not only compatible with
ourWi-Firouters;and(ii)ourWi-FiroutersimportedtotheUnitedStatesremainunaffected,
primarily because (a) all products that obtained FCC certification prior to March 23, 2026
remain unaffected and continue to be shipped to customers without interruption; (b) all
ongoing projects involving us are proceeding as planned under existing certifications. These
projects fall within the exemption scope of the new regulation and are not subject to its
requirements. No disruption to project schedules or supply commitments has occurred; and
(c) we currently have no new projects being introduced into the U.S. market. Should any new
projects arise in the future, the conditional approval framework would provide a transition
period of up to 18 months. We will evaluate on a case-by-case basis whether to apply for such
conditional approval; and (iii) we currently do not possess local manufacturing capabilities
within the United States. If future regulatory or commercial conditions necessitate such
capabilities, we will conduct a formal feasibility assessment and will keep the relevant
regulatory authorities informed as appropriate. In addition, we will implement the following
mitigating measures in response to the current regulatory framework. Specifically, (a) we will
utilize our existing portfolio of FCC certified products to ensure uninterrupted shipments to
the U.S. market; (b) for any potential future U.S. projects, we will assess the necessity of
applying for conditional approval and, where appropriate and utilize the available 18 month
transition period; and (c) we will maintain strategic and operational flexibility, monitor
market and regulatory developments, and evaluate potential U.S. based manufacturing plans
if needed. For the related risk, see “Risk Factors — Risks Relating to Our Industry and
Business—Ourbusiness,financialconditionandresultsof operationsmaybemateriallyand
adversely affected by international policies and international export controls and economic
sanctions.”

BUSINESS
Digital Video Device
Media streaming terminals
Our media streaming terminals are core devices for home users to access TV, glasses,
and other displays. They connect to the display screens, through which home users can select
theirpreferred4KTVprogramsfromawidearrayof differenttypes,anduseinternetservice,
such as online shopping and gaming. We were one of the first companies in China to secure a
Google Android TV certification in 2017, according to Frost & Sullivan. Furthermore, we
weretheworld’slargestAndroidTVsmartterminalsupplierintermsof salesvolumein2024,
according to the same source. The main customers of our streaming media terminals are
telecom operators, retailers and certain other smart home product providers.
Our media streaming terminals are equipped with the Google Android TV system,
enabling access to Google Play Store’s content ecosystem, fulfilling the demand of overseas
end-users for a vast array of internet video content. In terms of functionality, our products
integrate hardware-accelerated video decoding technology and support AI super-resolution,
enabling real-time upscaling of standard-definition video images to 4K resolution, delivering
clearer and smoother visual effects for users. Additionally, our media streaming terminals
feature built-in decoding modules for multiple digital TV signal formats, including different
protocolsincludingDVB/ATSC/ISDB-T,supportingreceptionof broadcastsignalsinvarious
regions. Our terminals also offer enhanced usability through interactive features such as
Bluetooth and voice remote control, and, furthermore, they can be connected to our
self-developed system platform Cedar (Home AI Agent), which can execute lightweight AI
algorithms on the terminal side to achieve real-time image enhancement, voice interaction
processing,environmentperception,andotherfunctions,creatingpersonalizedentertainment
services that better understand users.
Our media streaming terminals come in a variety of forms. In addition to traditional
OTT TV boxes, we have launched Dongle and Stick, which are portable devices with exquisite
designs, catering to the needs of users who require a more portable product. To create a
high-end smart entertainment experience, we have also integrated OTT TV boxes with
speakers to launch smart speaker products with media streaming content access. These
products are capable of running AI algorithms, and are also equipped with our voice AI
models embeded in our Cedar, enabling interaction with households to conduct various
voice-controlledactivities,suchascontentplaybackandswitchingon/off homeappliances.In
recent years, to respond the growing demand for screen-free viewing, we have also introduced
the XR Station, which can empower conventional AR glasses, allowing them to access to a
vast array of internet video content.
Smart projectors
Our smart projectors are integrated with media streaming terminals to display content
on projector screen or wall directly, eliminating the need for external displays. We were the
first ODM company worldwide to secure a Google TV projector certification in 2023,
according to Frost & Sullivan. The main customers of our projectors are retailers and certain
other smart home product providers.
Our smart projector is equipped with the Google TV smart operating system, enabling
users to easily access streaming apps and enjoy thousands of licensed content from Netflix,
YouTube, Prime Video, and more. It also features prevalent projection display technologies
such as LCD/DLP. We have a comprehensive product portfolio for DLP and LCD, from
low-end to high-end products, with brightness ranging from approximately 200 to 3000
lumens,allowinguserstoenjoyacomprehensive,immersive,andintelligentvisualexperience.
Our smart projector are also known for its portable size and a large projection screen, while
– 165 –

=== PAGE 175 ===
BUSINESS
supporting multiple input methods such as HDMI, USB, and Wi-Fi, allowing users to easily
connect smart devices and enjoy rich multimedia content. In addition, we have also launched
an ultra-short-throw projector that provides users with excellent image quality with a wide
color gamut and high contrast.
OurAIall-sceneadaptivesystemutilizesAIalgorithmssuchassecond-levelauto-focus,
auto-trapezoidal correction, intelligent eye protection, and real-time obstacle avoidance to
achieve environmental awareness and precise image adaptation, significantly enhancing the

ecosystem of “hardware + algorithms + content” to drive innovation and empowering the
smart projector industry while creating long-term value for global home users.
Smart cameras
Our smart cameras feature enhanced capabilities that include high-definition video
recordings,motiondetection,application-specificinformationcapturing,andreal-timealerts.
Equipped with processing chips and a rich library of trained algorithms, our smart
cameras may perform a variety of advanced functions and perfect synchronization with our
ecosystem. In addition to its software computing capabilities, high-definition lenses,
large-aperture sensors, and AI-ISP algorithm allow our smart cameras to capture
high-definition images with no noise, capturing every detail in daytime and at night.
Withregardtothenetworkfunctionsof oursmartcameras,ourcamerasarecompatible
withcloudstorage,effectivelymitigatingdatalossresultingfromdevicetheftandstoragecard
damages. Our speakers and microphones allow users to engage in high-quality, dual-way
online voice calls. Furthermore, our smart cameras can be connected with our self-developed
Cedar which allows real-time analysis of captured videos and seamless synchronization with
other digital video devices through voice command prompts and automatic settings.
The main customers of our camera products are telecom operators and retailers.
Network Communication Devices
Wi-Fi router
Wi-Fi router is a critical component of a home network, transferring internet signal to
wireless network that can be accessed through devices such as cell phones and computers. We
offer Wi-Fi routers supporting continuously evolving generations of Wi-Fi technology
includingWi-Fi5,6,and7,offeringacontinuouslyimprovingexperiencewithrespecttodata
flow and connection stability. With a full range of technology upgrades, our Wi-Fi routers
empowers the home network to enter a new generation of higher speed and greater
intelligence. Our Wi-Fi 7 has the advantage of low latency and high bandwidth, with a
maximum bandwidth of 19,000Mbps. In addition to its speed, our Wi-Fi routers are also
integratedwithMeshtechnology,allowingawiderangeof coverage,coveringtheentirehome
with Internet access.
As a critical component of our network communication devices, our Wi-Fi routers’
built-in channel scanning and anti-jamming algorithms, providing a more stable and faster
connection environment for a large number of IoT devices. Furthermore, our Wi-Fi sensing
algorithm allows our Wi-Fi routers to sense the surrounding environment through Wi-Fi
signals, enabling future functions such as illegal intrusion detection, resident health
monitoring and home energy saving. To further improve the experience of key applications,
our Wi-Fi router also features QoS traffic management and edge AI processing technology,

Optical network terminal and cable modems

technological upgrade allows users to enjoy symmetrical upstream and downstream 10G
network experience, meeting the demand for higher bandwidth while better adapting to

XHome: home device management platform
XHome is a one-stop home device management platform designed for operators and
retail brands. Its core features include a home device management platform, client app, and
smart device access SDK, providing access to XHome for our self-developed smart hardware
and Matter-compliant devices. At the same time, it can seamlessly set up a prevalent smart
home device ecosystem, helping operators and retail brands to quickly build a unified, open
and secure smart home platform, and realize multi-brand, multi-device interoperability and
personalized customization services.

Our XHome features the following core functionalities:
• Device management platform: XHome serves as the management platform,
responsible for unified smart device integration, remote control, operational
management, and data analysis. It supports device lifecycle management, bulk
OTA updates, fault monitoring and alerts, and intelligent scene linkage. This
enables efficient and secure management of home devices, providing a stable and
reliable cloud-based foundation for device control.
• Client App: XHome offers various functions to home users, including device
addition, remote control, scene linkage, household management, and alert
notifications. It also seamlessly integrates third-party agents or applications,
such as Google Home and Amazon Alexa, allowing home users to conveniently
controlalltheirsmartdeviceswithaunifiedapp.Thiscreatesaunified,intuitive,
and intelligent entry point for home device control.
• Smart Device Integration SDK: The XHome Smart Device Integration SDK
provides standardized access capabilities for proprietary and third-party smart
hardware.Itsupportsdeviceregistration,authentication,securecommunication,
and command transmission, compatible with various IoT protocols (e.g., Wi-Fi,
BLE, Matter). This accelerates and secures device integration into the XHome
platform, building a rich and open ecosystem.
EmpoweredbythedeepsynergiesamongCedar,XHome,andtheMatterecosystem,we
have achieved not only rapid integration and unified management of Matter-compliant
devices but also remove the integration barriers between different brands and platforms.
Leveraging Cedar’s AI capabilities in device perception, intelligent inference, and adaptive
scenes, we have created a cross-brand and cross-platform intelligent interaction experience,
fully empowering the end-to-end smart home product, making smart homes more proactive,
intuitive, and continuously evolving.

commissioning services significantly modify or customize the goods, therefore, the products
and the services are highly interrelated and combined as one single performance obligation
which is satisfied at a point in time. See “Financial Information — Material Accounting
Policies and Estimates — Revenue Recognition — Sales of Products.”

R&D Process
Wedevelopourproducts,solutionsandtechnology,takingintoconsiderationprimarily
operators’business needs and market trends and demands. Our R&D activities also focus on
satisfying certification requirements from various industry players, including those
certifications in connection with ecosystem, content, and technology.
Our R&D product design and development process typically consists of five stages:
Conceptual Phase: We assess the concept, feasibility, and market acceptance of the
product. Upon approval, the project is launched and enters the R&D process;
Planning Phase: We analyze the product’s functions and features, create a product
requirement traceability matrix, and conduct a preliminary design. We identify the
development workflow, break it down into manageable tasks, and develop a feasible
implementation plan;
Development Phase: Based on the product requirements, we conduct hardware design,
exterior design, structural design, software design, manufacturability, material selection,
procurement cycle and overall cost analysis and review. We then develop engineering
prototypes to ensure that the new product’s performance meets our requirements. During the
product design process, we refine and/or modify the product design and conduct rigorous
testing to ensure it meets the specification requirements;
Validation Phase: We conduct various certification tests on the product to ensure it
meets market access requirements. We also validate the product’s manufacturability to ensure
production efficiency for mass production;
Release Phase: We optimize production processes to ensure a stable manufacturing
process and mass production capability before commencing full-scale production.

PRODUCTION
We focus on product and solutions design and development as well as production
process design, which are crucial to our competitiveness. We outsource production and
manufacturing of our products to specialized original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to
secure stable production capacity, guarantee timely delivery, and achieve our sustainability
goals. Given the maturity of production technologies and the availability of sufficient
professional OEM vendors in the smart home industry, our adoption of a full outsourcing
model can ensure stable production capacity, good quality, and reduced costs. Under this
model, we usually procure raw materials, such as chips, storage units, modules and PCB, and
supply them to OEM vendors for manufacturing. We believe this enables us to better control
the quality of raw materials and improve customer satisfaction with the end products. In
addition, through centralized procurement of raw materials, we believe we are able to
negotiate with suppliers for more favorable prices. After the raw materials are delivered, the
OEMvendorswillproceedwiththeproductionprocess.Asof December31,2025,weengaged
16 OEM vendors, the majority of which were located in China and some were located in
Thailand, Vietnam and Poland.
We enter into framework agreements with our OEM vendors, and make specific orders
basedonourproductionplan,ourinventoryof rawmaterials,vendors’capacity,andoursales
orders and forecasts, among others. We are generally responsible for R&D and design of our
products (including software and hardware) based on our customers’ demands, as well as
sourcingmostof therawmaterialsneededforproductionof ourproducts,whereasourOEM
vendors are required to have the necessary production know-know, facilities and manpower
for production of our products. We will provide our OEM vendors with the raw materials
sourced by us, bill of materials, production requirements and testing software for production
purposes. We require vendors to follow our quality standards and delivery schedules, and
conduct final product acceptance procedures in accordance with the agreements and orders.
Such arrangement ensures stable production capacity and product supply and quality.
The below is a summary of the salient terms of the framework agreements and orders
with our OEM vendors.
• Term. Typically one to three years.
• Payment. Typically bank transfer.
• Credit Term. Typically 30 to 90 days.
• Delivery.Absentunusualcircumstanceswearerequiredtocollectourgoodsfrom
our OEM vendor’s location. Our OEM vendor may be required to deliver the
goods in special circumstances and we will be obliged to cover the fees in such
circumstances.
• Inspection and Acceptance. Our OEM vendors are typically obliged to conduct
product quality inspections according to our instructions and are obliged to
reach a 100% pass rate for the products to be delivered to us.
• RiskAllocation.Theriskistypicallytransferredtousatthetimeof ourreceiptof
the goods.
• IP. We maintain all IP rights over which we have ownership.

exhibitions and one-on-one marketing efforts. Our typical transaction process with telecom
operators involves the following stages:
• Tender Preparation Phase
o Demand Confirmation and Project Initiation: Identification of core
information including products, technical parameters, quantity, delivery
timeline, and service requirements;
o Tender Document Preparation: Formulation of the tender plan and
documents, and determination of the tender method.
– 179 –

=== PAGE 189 ===
BUSINESS
• Tender Publication Phase
o Publication of Tender Notice: For public tenders, notices are published
simultaneously on the telecom operator’s proprietary procurement
platform. The notices typically set forth the project name, products,
supplier qualification requirements, method for obtaining tender
documents, tender submission deadline, and bid opening location, among
others;
o Clarifications and Addenda: Potential suppliers submit any queries
regarding the tender documents to the telecom operator’s procurement
department before the query deadline.
The core objective of this phase is to ensure transparency of information so that
potential suppliers have equal access to tender information.
• Bid Response Phase
This phase is driven by potential suppliers. The core is to provide a complete
response as required, demonstrating compliance with qualifications and
competitiveness. Our R&D, procurement, production and sales departments revolve
around addressing clients’ customized requirements, with each stage being closely
interconnected.
• Bid Opening and Contract Award Phase
The telecom operator announces the bid-winning supplier and the two parties
enter into contracts.
• Post-Award Business Process
Following a successful bid award, we formulate a new product development plan
based on client requirements and produce trial prototypes. Upon client approval of the
prototypes, the client places a formal order. We then proceed to formulate production
plans,organizerawmaterialprocurement,andarrangeproduction.Afterproductionis
completed and products pass quality inspection, we deliver the products. Telecom
operators do not further modify the products purchased from us before selling them to
end users.
Although our customer base is relatively concentrated in telecom operators, we
do not rely on any single operator or a limited few. Instead, we engage in extensive
collaboration with telecom operators worldwide, and our major operator clients have
varied across different years during the Track Record Period. Moving forward, we will
continue to diversify our customer portfolio by actively pursuing partnerships with
retailers,traders,andothertypesof clients.Thisstrategywillhelpbroadenourrevenue
streams and mitigate the risks associated with over-reliance on any single customer
category.

Commercialization and Pricing Strategy
Wewillcontinuetofocusonourmajormarkets,suchasEurope,AmericasandAsia.In
addition to our existing products, such as digital video devices, network communication
devices and system platforms, we will further develop and sell AI-powered products, such as
AI glasses, robots and AI computing boxes, based on customer needs. Among these products,
our speakers have been preliminarily verified by our customers and are ready to be launched.
These products are expected to be launched in Americas first, and gradually promoted to
other major markets around the world. Other products, such as AI glasses, robots and AI
computingboxes,arestillintheresearchanddevelopmentstage.Wewillpromotethesalesof
these products based market demand after they are launched.
Wepriceourproductsbasedonavarietyof factors,including:(i)customerandmarket
factors, including (a) purchase volume: customers with large annual purchase volumes
typically receive more competitive pricing, (b) customer’s bargaining power: customers with
multiplesupplieroptionsoftenhavestrongerbargainingpowerandcansecuremorefavorable
prices, (c) sales channel: prices through traders are generally lower than direct sales to end
customers to leave reasonable profit margins for traders, and (d) regional market
characteristics: variations in operational expenses, tax policies, and market competition
across regions also directly affect local pricing strategies; (ii) product and service factors,
including (a) hardware configuration and performance: differences in core configurations
such as memory, modules, and interfaces can lead to significant cost variations, and (b)
software, content and service package: the price of digital video devices is often tied to
embeddedexclusivecontentservices,andquotationsfornetworkcommunicationdevicesmay
includesoftwarelicensesaswellastechnicalsupport,installation,andlongtermmaintenance
services; and (iii) strategic and cost factors, including (a) market competition and strategic
objectives: to enter new markets or respond to competition, we may offer “strategical prices”
to specific customers, where pricing is driven primarily by market objectives rather than cost
alone, and (b) dynamic cost structure: periodic fluctuations in raw material prices and
additional costs arising from dedicated production capacity arrangements or special logistics
to meet specific customer requirements are reflected in the final quotation.
– 188 –

=== PAGE 198 ===
BUSINESS
Asourproductsarehighlycustomized,pricingof comparableproductsonthemarketis
usually not publicly available. To ensure the market competitiveness and reasonableness of
our pricing, we keenly perceive market trends and obtain crucial pricing guidance through (i)
direct feedback from customers: as we regularly engage in price discussions and negotiations
with key customers, the market condition, price expectation, or pricing pressure disclosed by
customers during these communications provide us with the most direct, firsthand
information on market trends; (ii) analysis of order fluctuations: by continuously monitoring
changes in customer order volumes and, after excluding factors such as fluctuations in the
customer’s demand, if an unexpected decline in orders is observed, it may indicate that
competitors are offering more cost-effective alternatives. This suggests that our pricing is
likely facing market challenges; and (iii)assessment of the competitive landscape: domestic
players generally tend to adopt more aggressive pricing strategies to capture market share.
Therefore, launch of functionally similar products by domestic competitors is an indication
that they may enter the market with lower prices. This provides a key regional market
reference for our pricing strategy.
Specifically, we price our hardware products (including digital video devices, network
communication devices, and parts and accessories on a “cost plus”basis. For our XMediaTV
sold separately, (i) we charge a one-off fee based on the number of functional modules
subscribed by customers, with a price range of US$10,000 to US$500,000 and the average
sellingpricepercustomerof approximatelyUS$250,000duringtheTrackRecordPeriod,and
(ii) we charge periodic license fees based on the number of active users, with a price range of
US$499toUS$19,499duringtheTrackRecordPeriod.ForourXHomesoldseparately,(i)we
chargeaone-off feebasedonthenumberof functionalmodulessubscribedbycustomers,(ii)
we charge periodic license fees based on the number of active users, and (iii) we charge a
license fee for IoT equipment used. Our Cedar can be sold either as a built-in feature of our
hardwareproductsorseparatelyasasystemplatform.DuringtheTrackRecordPeriodandup
totheLatestPracticableDate,wehadnotsoldCedarseparatelyasasystemplatform.Forour
system platforms sold as a bundle with hardware products, we do not price the system
platforms separately, and instead we factor in the added value of our system platforms in the
pricing of the hardware products. Once we set the base prices according to these factors, we
adjust the pricing on a case-by-case basis in consideration of specific requirements of our
customers. We generally adopt the same pricing strategy for different customers regardless of
their geographical location.
PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT
Raw Materials and Procurement
Weprocurefromsuppliersavarietyof materialsnecessaryforthemanufacturingof our
products, including master control chips, memory chips, flash memory chips, function chips,
modules, remote control, power adapter, PCB board, and power cords.
We have preemptively established a qualified supplier database in reference to our
procurement plans. Our procurement plans are formulated based on production schedules,
inventory levels, supplier lead time and raw material’s lifetime. After the procurement plans
are approved, our supply chain management department will select the optimal supplier from
the supplier database by referring to factors including prices, quality, services, and delivery
time. As a consideration factor, the price will be determined through market research,
inquiries with the supplier or a competitive bidding process. We typically establish a
reasonable price with our suppliers through a process of inquiry or competitive bidding,
based on thorough market research. During the Track Record Period, the framework
agreements we entered into with our suppliers set out the standards and procedures to be
followed in future transactions, reflecting the parties’ intention to establish a cooperative
relationship over a certain period. Such framework agreements generally include basic terms
– 189 –

=== PAGE 199 ===
BUSINESS
suchasforecast-basedstockpreparation,procurementcycle,deliveryandacceptance,pricing
principles, settlement methods, payment terms, quality standards and requirements,
ownership of intellectual property, confidentiality obligations, liability for breach of
contract, and term of cooperation, but do not include specific material specifications,
quantities, or prices. In response to the potential price increases, we primarily mitigate the
impact on our raw material costs by building long-term relationships with our suppliers,
maintaining close communication and preemptively stocking critical materials. We have
internal mechanisms to monitor the price of our raw materials by considering current stock
levels, customer needs and market trends, among others. Specifically, to ensure stable supply
of our raw materials, we have implemented the following concrete measures: (a) Supplier
management: we adopt management strategies such as multi-source procurement, a four-tier
classificationsystem,andstrategiccooperationtodiversifyprocurementrisksandestablisha
stable and collaborative supply ecosystem. For each raw material category, we maintain at
least three primary suppliers and two alternative suppliers. Qualified suppliers are managed
underafour-tiersystem:strategic,preferred,general,andconditional.Weestablishlong-term
and close cooperative relationships with strategic suppliers. (b) Inventory management: we
establish mechanisms such as safety stock, capacity locking, and strategic inventory to
mitigate risks of short-term fluctuations and supply disruptions. Differentiated safety stock
standardsaresetfordifferentcategoriesof rawmaterialsandaredynamicallyadjustedbased
on market fluctuations. For key raw materials, we develop annual supplier cooperation plans,
defining annual procurement demand, technology upgrade plans, and delivery lead time
requirements.Weholdquarterlybusinessreviewmeetingswithstrategicsuppliersonaregular
basis, and based on the rolling forecasts provided by us, our suppliers arrange advance
stocking and lock production capacity to ensure supply. When prices are relatively low, we
opportunistically build strategic inventories to address potential future supply shortages or
significant price increases. (c) Technical measures: we pursue technical alternatives for key
materials, such as compatibility adaptation, energy consumption optimization, and
performance improvement, to reduce reliance on single sources and ensure supply continuity.
Wetimelyadjustourstocklevelstomaintainoptimalinventorylevelsconsideringanticipated
price fluctuations. In addition, during the Track Record Period, prices of our core raw
materials such as master control chips, memory chips and flash memory chips experienced
increases. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not
adopted any hedging policies for fluctuations in the prices of raw materials.

Supplier Management
We typically engage experienced suppliers within the industry with a well-established,
ISO 9001-certified management system that possess strong capabilities in design, R&D,
productionmanagement,andqualityassurancetoensurethequalityof ourproducts.Factors
that may affect our selection mainly include technological expertise, financial condition,
product quality, qualifications and credentials, reputation and price.

=== PAGE 204 ===
BUSINESS
We implement stringent supplier management mechanisms. Prospective suppliers must
undergostagesincludinginformationcollection,qualificationreviewandverification,on-site
reviewbythereviewteam,andremediesof issuesbeforebeingincludedinourlistof qualified
suppliers.If theprospectivesupplierpassestheaforementionedprocess,wewillfurtherobtain
product samples for an in-detail inspection.
In addition to vetting new suppliers, we evaluate the quality of goods provided by our
suppliers on a monthly and annual basis and require suppliers to promptly address any issues
discovered during such evaluations. We require suppliers who fail to meet our standards to
implement corrective measures.
Wetypicallyenterintoframeworksupplyagreementsandspecificorderswithsuppliers,
the salient terms of which are set out below:
• Duration. The duration of the framework supply agreements typically lasts
indefinitely until terminated by either party.
• Product specifications. We specify the product name, manufacturer or brand,
specification, price, quantity, delivery timeline and other detailed items in each
purchase order we send to our suppliers.
• Payment, credit term and delivery. The suppliers are typically responsible for the
delivery of products to our designated location specified in each purchase order.
In terms of payment, we are generally granted by our suppliers a credit term of
one to six months following our acceptance of the goods and the finalization of
the invoice.
• Transfer of risk. The risk transfers to us after we complete inspection and
confirm receipt of the products.
• Quality Guarantee. In the event of a quality issue arising during the warranty
period, the supplier is obliged to either attend the site or provide a response and
resolution upon receipt of our notification.
• Subcontracting.Subcontractingisnotallowedwithoutwrittenconsentfromboth
parties.
• Confidentiality.Thesuppliershallnotdiscloseormakepublicthecontentsof the
purchase orders without our prior written consent.
• Productreturn.Wehavetherighttoreject,replaceorreturnproductsforavariety
of reasons, including non-conformity with product quality, product
specifications or quantity with the order placed.
• Termination. We are entitled to terminate the purchase order when the supplier
failstoperformanddoesnotmaketimelycorrectionsafterreceiptof ourwritten
notice. Both parties may terminate the agreement by giving a written notice no
less than 30 days prior to the termination date.

INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
We attach great importance to our inventory health, assigning dedicated staff to
provide management with regular reports on the status of inventory. We take inventory level
into consideration when formulating procurement plans.
Our inventories mainly include raw materials, work-in-process and finished goods, and
goodsintransits.Wehavevariouspoliciesinplacetoensureeffectiveinventorymanagement,
such as adopting the first-in, first-out method, maintaining a safety stock to compensate for
anyunexpectedincreaseindemandordelayinsupplyandtrackingandmonitoringtheflowof
goods and inventory levels through our warehouse management system (“WMS”), which our
Directors believe are effective measures in managing our inventories. In 2023, 2024 and 2025,
our inventory turnover days were 83, 102 and 102 days, respectively. See “Financial
Information — Discussion of Certain Key Items from Consolidated Statements of Financial
Position — Inventories.” Among the raw materials we use, main control chips, memory and
flashstorageusuallyrequirearelativelylongerleadtimeof procurement,whichusuallytakes
three to six months and even nine months occasionally. We usually make prepayment for
ordering these raw materials in order to secure supply.

COMPETITION
The global smart home products for enterprise customers market is highly competitive
and the competitive landscape is relatively fragmented, with more than 200 market players in
the global smart home products for enterprise customers market, according to Frost &
Sullivan.Basedonthedifferentoperationmodels,themajorplayersintheglobalsmarthome
product market for enterprise customers can be further categorized into two types:
corporate-serving smart home product providers under the light moderation model and such
providers under the heavy operation model.
The light operation model features product design as their core competition strength
whileproductsinvolvedinsmarthomeproductsaremanufacturedthroughOEMs.Theheavy
operation model, in turn, refers to providers that manufacture their own products. Compared
with the heavy model, solution providers under the light model are more flexible. Providers
using the light models can choose production sites and co-production partners around the
worldaccordingtocustomers’needs,thusshorteningtheproductionanddeliverycycletothe
greatest extent possible while reducing the impact of geopolitical tension at the same time.
We adopted the asset-light production model in partnership with well-known OEMs
based in various countries and regions in the world. This unique model brings manufacturing
agility, allowing us to achieve economies of scale for large-volume orders, while maintaining
flexible production capacity for diverse, small-batch requests. Compared to other providers,
we enjoy the advantages of being an integrated smart home product provider for enterprise
customers. An integrated smart home product provider for enterprise customers can
continuously enrich and expand its product matrix by offering a wide spectrum of hardware,
infrastructure, and platform solutions, thereby addressing the diversified and evolving needs
of customers. In addition, an integrated smart home product provider for enterprise
customers can also create a seamless and interoperable ecosystem, which not only enhances
user experience by ensuring smooth connectivity and unified management but also enables
stronger customer stickiness through bundled solutions. We were the eighth largest provider
globally, and the third largest among Chinese Mainland-based providers, in the global smart
homeproductforenterprisecustomersmarketintermsof revenuein2024,accordingtoFrost
& Sullivan. In terms of market size in 2024, the global enterprise smart home product market
accounts for approximately 14.7% of the entire global smart home product market.

Inlightof thefollowingfactorsandcircumstances,andintheabsenceof anyemployee
complaintsregardingthismatter,ourPRCLegalAdvisorisof theopinionthatthelikelihood
of us incurring material administrative penalties for underpayment of social insurance and
housing provident funds contributions during the Track Record Period is remote:
(1) According to the Urgent Notice on Implementing the Spirit of the Executive
Meeting of the State Council and Effectively Stabilizing Social Insurance
PremiumCollectionWorkissuedbytheGeneralOfficeof theMinistryof Human
Resources and Social Security on September 21, 2018, authorities at all levels
responsible for collecting social insurance premiums are strictly prohibited from
conducting centralized recovery of historical arrears of enterprises on their own
initiative. The Notice of the State Taxation Administration on Implementing
Several Measures to Further Support and Serve the Development of the Private
Economy issued on November 16, 2018, and the Notice on Issuing the
Comprehensive Plan for Reducing Social Insurance Premium Rates issued by the
GeneralOfficeof theStateCouncilonApril1,2019,alsoemphasizedtheproper
handling of historical arrears of enterprises and prohibited centralized recovery
of such arrears during the reform of the collection system.
(2) Based on inquiries to the Shenzhen Social Insurance Fund Administration and
the Shenzhen Housing provident fund Management Center, which are the
competent authorities for the subject matter according to our PRC Legal
Advisors, both authorities confirmed that, with respect to enterprises’ failure to
make social insurance and housing provident fund contributions based on
employees’ actual wages, the competent authorities primarily focus on urging
enterprises to make up the shortfall for the specific employees who have filed
complaints or reports regarding their own underpaid contributions. There is
currently no specific enforcement policy for conducting comprehensive
investigations into the historical compliance of enterprises regarding social
insurance and housing provident fund contributions, or for requiring enterprises
to conduct centralized repayments of historical underpayments.
(3) As of the Latest Practicable Date, none of our employees had filed complaints
with the competent authorities regarding the aforementioned underpaid social
insurance and housing provident fund contributions, and there had been no
administrative penalties, investigations, or any labor disputes or conflicts with
our employees concerning social insurance or housing provident fund matters.
Furthermore, if the relevant authorities order us to make full social insurance
and/or housing provident fund payments or to take remedial measures in
accordance with applicable laws and regulations, we will promptly make the
relevant payments or take such remedial measures within the specified period.
(4) Based on the Public Credit Information Report on No Illegal or Non-compliant
Records and the Public Credit Information Inquiry Report (No Illegal or
Non-compliant Records Version) queried by our Company and our PRC
subsidiaries, during the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable
Date, our Company and our PRC subsidiaries had no record of illegal or
non-compliant activities or administrative penalties in relation to social
insurance and housing provident fund contributions.

insurance and housing provident fund contributions for all employees and had discontinued
theuseof third-partyagenciesforsuchwithholdingandremittanceservices.Underapplicable
laws and regulations, employers are principally responsible for handling and paying social
insurance and housing provident fund contributions for their employees. According to our
PRC Legal Advisors, our previous practice of using third-party agencies to make these
contributions, without directly completing the social insurance registration procedures or
establishing housing provident fund accounts for the relevant employees, constituted a
procedural imperfection. The maximum liability that we may potentially be subject to for
paying social insurance and housing provident fund contributions through third-party
agencies is RMB0.12 million. Nevertheless, by making contributions through third-party
agencies, we substantively fulfilled our legal obligation to provide social insurance and
housingprovidentfundcoverageforouremployees.Thisapproachalignswiththepurposeof
theSocialInsuranceLawof thePeople’sRepublicof Chinainprotectingthelegitimaterights
andinterestsof employees,andtheinterestsof ouremployeeswerenotmateriallyprejudiced.
Based on the Public Credit Information Report on No Illegal or Non-compliant Records and
thePublicCreditInformationInquiryReport(NoIllegalorNon-compliantRecordsVersion)
queriedbyourCompanyandourPRCsubsidiaries,duringtheTrackRecordPeriodandupto
the Latest Practicable Date, our Company and our PRC subsidiaries had no record of illegal
or non-compliant acts or administrative penalties in relation to social insurance and housing
provident fund contributions. As a result, no provision has been made for this incident.
As advised by our PRC Legal Advisors, save for the aforementioned incidents, we were
in compliance with applicable laws and regulations related to social insurance and housing
provident funds in all material aspects during the Track Record Period.
In light of the foregoing, our Directors are of the view that these incidents related to
social insurance and housing provident fund contributions would not have any material
adverse impact on our Group’s business, financial condition or results of operations.
We will, to the extent required and as soon as practicable upon receiving any
notificationfromtherelevantgovernmentauthoritiesrequiringustomakeupfortheshortfall
amounts or amend our policies or practices in this regard, make full contributions in
accordance with relevant PRC laws and regulations. This is to ensure that we will not be
subject to administrative penalties from the relevant government authorities due to failure to
make timely contributions.
Inanefforttomakefullcontributionstotheextentpossibleandassoonaspracticable,

RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL
We face various risks in the course of our daily operations. We have established a
comprehensive internal control and risk management system designed to address the
operational, financial, legal, and market risks inherent in our business. This system is
regularly reviewed and updated to ensure its effectiveness, alignment with our operational
needs, and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. Our internal controls cover
key functions such as sales, procurement, production, inventory management, and quality
control.
Internal Control System
Ourriskmanagementpolicycoversallkeyaspectsof operations.TheAuditCommittee,
established under the Board of Directors, is responsible for overseeing risk management and
internal controls. Our senior management team and our internal audit department are
responsible for the day-to-day execution of these internal control procedures. We also
regularly review relevant policies and procedures to ensure they comply with regulatory
requirements and business objectives.
Financial Reporting Risk Management
Our accounting policies cover budgeting, financial statement preparation, and
accounting record management. We have implemented a multi-layered review mechanism,
including segregation of duties, hierarchical approval authorities, and automated accounting
systems,toenhancetheintegrityof financialdata.Toguardagainstfraudulentreporting,our
finance department conducts regular internal audits and engages independent external
auditors to assess financial reporting risks. Our finance department also evaluates internal
